endings.title: The Lamp Lit
text: Maelis lifted the crown from her own head and broke it across the anvil of her ancestors. Cindrath died screaming in the stone, and the mountain let out a long, slow breath.
By spring the Kiln had cooled into hot springs, all the way down to the Grayflow.

endings.title: The Last Varrow
text: Corin put the crown on just long enough to break it from the inside. Cindrath went out like a snuffed wick, and so did the ember in his blood: he never cast another spell.
Varrow's Mill turns again. Two Varrows run it now, and they argue about the price of flour every single day.

endings.title: The Lamp Snuffed
text: You struck Maelis down, then the thing that had waited inside her crown. The mountain quieted. Ashford survived.
Nobody in town ever learned the whole truth about the Varrows, unless you told them.

endings.title: The Ember Queen
text: The crown closed on Maelis's head and Cindrath wore her like a coat. You killed what she became.
It was a victory. It didn't feel like one. The mountain cooled, and nobody floated a lantern for her.

endings.title: The Ember Heir
text: Cindrath found the ember in Corin's blood and climbed in. Nobody reached him in time.
You put out the fire, and the boy it was burning in. Maelis was not there to see it. Perhaps that was a mercy.

endings.title: The Ember Crown
text: You set the crown on your own head. The mountain obeys you now; the forges burn at your word, and Ashford pays its tithe in coal and quiet.
You don't remember your name. The voice remembers it for you.

endings.title: The Guild's Prize
text: You handed the shards to Captain Kell, and Kell handed them to the Coinwright Guild, because that was the contract.
In Waterdeep, a counting-house keeps a crown in a lead-lined vault. The moneylenders have a weapon now. Somewhere, it is warm.

letters.title: Thirty-One
paragraphs: The springs are warm all the way down to the river now. Brannoc charges outsiders a silver to sit in them and calls it "a cure." It cures nothing. They pay anyway. I've started keeping his ledger.
Come back for Lantern Night. Bring the goblin. Bring your lanterns. I'll bake the bread, and I'll burn the bottoms.

letters.title: If You're Reading This
paragraphs: If you're reading this, then you were right, and I'm glad it was you.
Float one for me if they'll let you. If they won't, float one anyway. The river doesn't ask whose they are.

letters.title: Unsent
letters.note: Found in the Kiln after the fight, the last thing she wrote before the crown took her.

slides.title: Ashford
slides.text: Hadric Varrow's name was read out in the square again, this time with an apology. On Lantern Night the town floated thirty-one lanterns, not thirty.

slides.title: Ashford
slides.text: Brannoc stood in the square and said what he had signed, and why. The town floated thirty-one lanterns that winter.

slides.title: Ashford
slides.text: Ashford rebuilt, and floated thirty lanterns again, as it always had. Nobody said Hadric Varrow's name.

slides.title: The Drowned Lantern
slides.text: Brannoc never left his inn. When the hot springs came, the Drowned Lantern was suddenly the most fashionable house in the valley. He hates it. He has raised his prices twice.

slides.title: The Drowned Lantern
slides.text: Brannoc went downriver with the boats and came back in the spring to find his inn still standing, full of ash and one very smug cat. He reopened it in a week.

slides.title: Edric
slides.text: Edric runs the Hall's messages now, in a very fine pair of boots. He tells the ledger story every market day, and it gets longer every time.

slides.title: Brother Ulric
slides.text: Ulric spent the rest of his days getting the Collapse widows their pensions, one Guild clerk at a time. He and Brannoc drink together on Lantern Night and don't talk about the mine.

slides.title: Brother Ulric
slides.text: Every Lantern Night, Brannoc floats an extra lantern for Ulric Dunmore and doesn't say who it's for.

slides.title: Tamsin
slides.text: Tamsin went back to her grandmother's herbs and turned out to have a better hand for them than Old Wynn, which Wynn will never admit.

slides.title: Tamsin
slides.text: Tamsin's notes from inside the Hollow Star are how the town found the Star's widows and paid them what they were owed.

slides.title: Captain Kell
slides.text: Kell brought every one of his soldiers home, which he says is the only contract that matters. He sends a crate of Waterdeep wine to the Lantern every Midwinter.

slides.title: Captain Kell
slides.text: Kell told the Guild the shards were destroyed, which was true by the time he said it. He took a smaller fee and a longer road home.

slides.title: Captain Kell
slides.text: Kell counted his dead, filed his report, and never came back to the Grayflow.

slides.title: Mayor Tarrow
slides.text: Tarrow lives in two rooms over the cooper's yard and keeps the town's books for free. Some mornings someone leaves bread on his step. Some mornings they don't.

slides.title: Mayor Tarrow
slides.text: They say Oswin Tarrow keeps a clerk's desk in Waterdeep now, and is very sorry in a comfortable room.

slides.title: Mayor Tarrow
slides.text: Ashford buried its mayor quietly. The town council still argues about whose fault that was.

slides.title: Wix
slides.text: Wix opened a pie stall by the new springs. It is very popular. Nobody asks where the pies come from, and Wix offers no proverbs on the subject.

slides.title: The Coinwright Guild
slides.text: Nessa's sworn statement reached the Guild's counting-house in Waterdeep. A debt built on a forged report is an awkward thing to collect in court, so the Guild quietly wrote off a third of what Ashford owed and called it generosity.

slides.title: Nessa Thorne
slides.text: Nessa burned both halves of her contract in Brannoc's hearth and stayed to watch the ash go cold. The songs say Cindrath died screaming in the stone. Nessa knows better, and she doesn't sing along.

slides.title: Nessa Thorne
slides.text: Nessa turned down the best price she will ever be offered. Her contract is still in her satchel, and on bad nights she takes it out and reads clause nine again. On good nights she doesn't.

slides.title: Nessa Thorne
slides.text: Every Midwinter a letter comes for Nessa in grey ink, with no return address: her account, still open. She went back to reading contracts for a living, looking for something worth more than a soul.

slides.title: Corin
slides.text: Corin stayed for Lantern Night, and the one after that. He and Maelis still don't agree about anything, loudly, over burnt honey-bread.

slides.title: Harl
slides.text: Harl Deepdelve keeps Moradin's shrine below the Old Mine again. Every shift that goes down hears thirty-one names read out first, and the last of them is Hadric Varrow's.

slides.title: Harl
slides.text: Harl went back to the dwarf halls in the west. Every Lantern Night he sends a letter to Ashford with thirty-one names in it, and asks Brannoc to read them aloud.

slides.title: The kindled
slides.text: The ember-kiss never quite faded. On cold nights the rings on your palms glow like coals, and once in a long while, just before sleep, something warm and patient says your name.

slides.title: The kindled
slides.text: By spring the red rings on your palms had faded to freckles. You never answered the voice in the dream, and in the end it stopped asking.

slides.title: Vorna Kalvaar
slides.text: Vorna carried four purses down the mountain herself and knocked on four doors. At the last one, Sef's mother made her stay for supper, and nobody in that house made a warding sign.

slides.title: Vorna Kalvaar
slides.text: The Guild never paid. Vorna went to Waterdeep and sat on the Coinwright Guild's front steps in her old grey cloak, every morning, until a clerk came out with four purses just to make her leave.

slides.title: The Voice
slides.text: Vorna never heard the voice again. Some nights she almost misses it, and that frightens her more than the dragon ever did. She sleeps fine.

slides.title: The Voice
slides.text: On cold nights Vorna still wakes up warm, sure that someone has just said "daughter" in the dark. She keeps a sword by the bed, pointed at the door.
